proposals.impact: lift open rates on Money Worship and Avoidance sequences toward Vigilance's 66.67% benchmark
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance emails are opening at 66.67% (8/12 sent). Money Worship sits at 37.5% (6/16). Money Avoidance is at 52.63% (10/19). That 29-percentage-point gap between Vigilance and Worship is not random — the Vigilance sequence likely uses a subject line that names a specific felt experience, whereas Worship probably gestures at a concept. The subject line is the single file-level change with the highest probabilistic return before any structural or content work.
proposals.proposal: Pull the subject line formula from the Money Vigilance email-1 subject and apply the same structural logic to Money Worship email-1. The Vigilance subject almost certainly names a concrete, recognisable internal moment rather than a money archetype label. Worship subscribers have demonstrated lower engagement from the first touch — fixing that subject line costs one file edit and could close most of the gap before the rest of the sequence even loads. Joel should read both subjects side by side, identify what Vigilance makes *visceral* that Worship only *labels*, then rewrite the Worship subject in that same register. The replacement text below is a worked example to be adjusted against the actual Vigilance subject once Joel reads it.
proposals.current_text: subject: Your Money Worship profile results
proposals.new_text: subject: You earned well this month. So why does checking your balance still feel like a threat?

proposals.observation: One post sits in the content queue. With the publish workflow broken (see Proposal 2), that single post is the only buffer between "consistent publishing" and a content gap. The three most recent posts all follow a "Why do I..." question format — a pattern that is working given the Money Avoidance open rates — but there is nothing staged behind the one queued post. proposals.proposal: Draft and commit one new "Why do I..." blog post targeting the Money Worship reader specifically, since that sequence has the weakest engagement and a content piece written from inside that psychology could both serve as a sequence touchpoint and a standalone SEO page. The post should use a question only a Worship-pattern reader would recognise as their own — not a generic money anxiety question. The draft below is a working title and opening paragraph; Joel should complete it from his own case notes.
proposals.new_text:
---
title: "Why do I feel proud of my salary but quietly ashamed of what I've actually done with it?"
pubDate: "2026-06-14"
draft: true
tags: ["money worship", "earning vs building"]
---

Joel here. There is a specific kind of discomfort that shows up in people who have worked hard to reach a good income — a number they once told themselves would feel like enough — and then found that the account balance tells a quieter story.

It is not overspending in any dramatic way. It is more like the money arrived and then... dispersed, without a clear decision being made. A few upgrades. Some subscriptions that accumulated. A holiday that felt deserved. And now there is a gap between the salary and what the savings actually say, and looking at that gap produces something that sits closer to shame than confusion.

That gap is not a character flaw. It is worth understanding as a pattern. Here is what I see in it, and what tends to sit underneath it.
